cohorts.summary: New players encounter automatic weapon firing and early character options.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that weapons fire automatically during gameplay.

citations.review_text: Grabbing a refund on this before I end up completely throwing away 10s - 100s of hours. I understand the appeal behind the genre very well, and the gameplay loop, particularly in this, is very satisfying. There's just not really much skill involved at all and I don't see any particular goals in the game to keep me interested, other than logging hours and hours into the game so that I can run around for longer, watching my character auto-attack more enemies. It's the virtual equivalent of doing stimulants and whacking off all day.

I stumbled about this genere by playing "Airships: Lost Flotilla", and I must say I do like it. Vampire Survivors is maybe a bit more stressful, or maybe the undead simply scare me, what do I know?. 
I really like the idea of auto firing weapons + roguelite decisions. 
And here I thought there was only Airships that played like this. well, theres also Brotato and Vampire Survivors, right? 
I realized this has been a whole genre for years now ... i feel stupid, I must admit.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features multiple characters and downloadable content options.

citations.review_text:
Though not the first survivaton like the game suggests, this game did popularize that genre. And despite how many survivatons there are now, this game holds up pretty well on its own. It's pretty addicting and fun, with lots of characters to try out and a ton of content to clear. That's not even counting DLCs. All for cheap too.

Big number go up

This hides the fact that it is an unapologetic grindfest rather well with a simple but effective gameplay loop of avoid enemies, pick up powerups. It leaves me wanting to experiment with new characters and in general play more than it does frustrate me so yeah, I think it's worth a play.

No comment on any of the DLC - I have not tried any of them yet. The base game is expansive enough that it gave me more than enough to chew on as of time of reviewing.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as requiring external guides or a wiki to discover hidden secrets and mechanics.

citations.review_text: I went into this game expecting maybe a couple hours of fun, similar to a flash game from the olden days. But there is so much more to this game than that, it almost feels endless with the amount of secrets and content there is to unlock. This game's entire design philosophy is built around being one of those obtuse games like Simon's Quest for NES, the kinda game you needed Nintendo Power for. So no only is there secrets galore to unlock, you also have to have the wiki on hand. Some may not like this, but i do. It harkens back to an older age, a better age, of gaming.

A hectic game of choice rather than a game of skill, a deceiptively simple core gameplay on top of which are progressively added strategic complexity and challenges as you progress through the stages and unlocks new characters, weapons, passives, etc ...

It is tremendously addictive, with a shower of visual and audio feedbacks as you turn into a monster mowing machine.

It might not be a fantastic looker, but I enjoy its relative simplicity and explosion of garish visual effect.
Also it runs on my potato of a laptop, so big plus for that.

The biggest obstacle to the enjoyment of this game for most people is probably going to be whether or not you adhere to the core gameplay loop of moving around, zig zaging through the waves of enemies while your weapons fire automatically.

It's a run based game, so, likewise, if that's not your jam ... this is not for you.
However unlike some other run based games, there is a great amount of permanent progression (which can be disabled for the most masochistic of us).
So, even if you fail, you *will* progress and be able to make your way through.

This is also a "wiki game", there is _a lot_ of informations that the game will hide from you, and that you will have to discover by yourself (which I love) ... or quickly find online.

I thoroughly recommend it.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game continues to receive regular content updates and cheap or free downloadable content.

citations.review_text:
Phenomenal! I didn't believe the reviews until i tried it.
It is not a money sink on the contrary 2 free DLCs and the rest are cheap.
The game receives regular updates. Highly recommended.

This game is a must-have for shorter play sessions, for a seemingly never-ending barrage of updates and DLC, and for supporting a truly worthwhile game. Years after its release, the base version keeps pumping content, and the price remains low and affordable. There's more meat here than there is in titles with 8x its price. The gameplay is fun and engaging, the character writing fun and funny, and the race for full completion remains ever-on.

claims.claim: This cohort reports that the initial 4 to 15 hours of the game can feel slow or excruciatingly difficult when attempting to push for new stages before unlocking basic upgrades and weapons.

citations.review_text:
I would recommend this game but with the understanding that it's for a very specific type of player.

If you like ball crushing challenge, this game probably isn't for you. Ironically, the first 10-15 hours of this game are excruciatingly difficult if you're trying to push for new stages, but after that point (or after downloading enough DLC) you eventually break the game and there's no putting the toothpaste back in the tube. Arcana cards alone are very game breaking once you have the good ones, but you can also permanently increase character stats between playthroughs with buyable Golden Eggs, you can use the Paranormal Scan from the Among Us DLC along with Endless mode to buff your stats even further beyond that, and you'll just be swimming in gold past a certain point to buy any character or powerup you want. The only real challenge at that point is the adventures, which have separate progress mostly from the rest of the game, but even in the adventures you will have access to your Arcana cards and you can pretty quickly break those too. It only takes me about 3 runs (a few failed) before I completely crack open an adventure from nothing and have unlimited gold and all my items back.

The kind of people this game is going to appeal to long term is completionist players. Once the game gets too easy, it becomes more about exploring the maps and figuring out how to go through the huge list of unlocks/in-game achievements and get the hard or obtuse ones with little direction to go off of. This is where I have the most fun with the game now, just seeing if I can actually clear this massive list of goals. I have all of the in-game achievements that correspond to Steam achievements (so from Steam's perspective I've perfect-ed the game) but that doesn't include like any of the DLC content or a lot of the really advanced Extra content.

So, if you're the kind of person that likes getting a big checklist and checking stuff off slowly and incrementally and getting ne…

Don't download the free Ante-Chamber DLC until you've completed the base game and all paid DLC because it totally destroys the games balance and trivializes any level of difficulty the game offers. 

Otherwise the game is fun and challenging and there's so many layers of depth with lots of different systems. There will be a period where you're waiting 10 minutes for the levels to end because you're so OP, but just keep completing different stages with different characters and the game will become more challenging and unfold new mechanics beyond your initial experience

I was positive I had recommended this game before. But oh well. 

Great game, the first 4-6 runs may be slow going, but once you start unlocking basic things you will see there is no real ending to the madness! Go for it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that visual effects and projectiles can fill the screen completely, leading to heavy sensory overload or potential issues for those sensitive to flashing lights.

citations.review_text:
one of the most "video gamey" video games i can think of. and i mean that in a good way.

extremely reasonably priced, DLCs too. perfect way to kill 30 min to an hour. has the "just one more run" factor. one of the most accessible games in recent memory. satisfying gameplay loop and progression.

prepare to have your eyes and dopamine receptors bleed.

Quite fun. Can take a bit to get rolling, but once you get all the stuff for a good build, you get to just watch number go up forever. Do note that the amount of effects on screen can become a bit overkill.

This game is SO FUN. I have played this game on my phone as well for hundreds of hours and it's still not boring! I will ALWAYS recommend this game to my friends because it's just so addicting. It starts off fun but after some time gets to the point where the screen is full of projectiles and you feel like you could kill god and not even notice. It somehow doesn't lag on my new or old PC and my phone handles it well too. Overall this is the best roguelike, and its an 10/10. Please buy it.

You know, the game may not take much brainpower or mechanical skill to play, but to be frank, sometimes all the entertainment you need is big numbers and sensory overload. Vampire Survivors delivers the feeling of being on a power trip in spades. Also, all the little jokes and references in the names/mechanics/bestiary are very nice.
An amazing way to kill time in the best way possible. Provided your not sensitive to flashing lights.

Between Steam and Game Pass, I've played over 200 hours of Vampire Survivors over the last few years. It's an absolutely ridiculous smack of dopamine to the brain that's insanely fun and unbelievably affordable (whether it's on sale or not). It continues to get massive free updates every year, and crazy cheap DLC packs, including one of the best Castlevania crossovers ever made. Highly recommended to both casual and hardcore gamers alike. Though definitely avoid if you have epilepsy. Seriously. LOTS of flashy effects.
Insane fun to play. Bright lights, flashing, pretty....what more is there to say?

Hear me out. 
I was so hesitant back in the day to play this one. 
I love games like this and i also really like nice cute or edgy graphics. 
And this one is pixels only. Not that i dont like that, 
lately i find myself enjoying some nice pixel-mush. 

But back then, i didnt. Eventually, when there werent many more Survivors-like games 
to find, i figured i'd might as well give it a try. 
Let me tell you - theres a reason those kinds of games are 
called 'Vampire-Survivors-like'. 
It is the mother and father of those games. 
It is pure dopamine (and grinding).

Would buy it over and over again, 
It keeps getting more and more content, 
its a steal. 

Its one of the best games to ever exist. 
(The other one is powerwash simulator.)
